sections.content: An opening gerund packs a method or condition into the front of a sentence (how someone achieved something, or what state they were in while doing it); a gerund can also sit inside a sentence as the complement of a verb like esperar. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Aprendiendo español con sorprendente rapidez, se convirtió en la intérprete y asesora estratégica de Cortés.
items.english: Learning Spanish with surprising speed, she became Cortés's interpreter and strategic advisor.

items.spanish: Sobreviviendo en circunstancias imposibles, tomó decisiones dentro de un margen de maniobra extremadamente limitado.
items.english: Surviving under impossible circumstances, she made decisions within an extremely limited margin for maneuver.

items.spanish: Reconociendo su contribución decisiva, la corona española concedió a Tlaxcala un estatus especial.
items.english: Recognizing its decisive contribution, the Spanish crown granted Tlaxcala special status.

items.spanish: Apoyaron activamente a los españoles esperando obtener mayor autonomía a cambio.
items.english: They actively supported the Spanish, hoping to gain greater autonomy in exchange.

sections.content: An opening gerund (Aprendiendo..., Sobreviviendo..., Reconociendo...) always describes something true about the sentence's main subject — check that the person doing the gerund and the person doing the main verb are the same, which they always are in Spanish, unlike some looser uses of '-ing' in English.
